body.x: Flooring laid for an exhibition or event takes heavy foot traffic and is often installed only for the length of the show, which raises the question of whether it can be used again afterward.
Bokwang Industry built its flooring product around that question.

Bokwang Industry Co., Ltd., an industrial nonwovens and functional composite materials manufacturer in the Gunwi Industrial Complex in Daegu, is led by CEO Malsoon Choi. At KES 2026, the company is exhibiting six products, beginning with Pytex exhibition and event flooring in plain, embossed and flame-retardant types and 17 colors, together with a non-slip roll mat with a TPE coating, a three-layer waterproof composite sheet, a geotextile nonwoven that meets Korean Industrial Standards (KS), a weed-control sheet and a cushion sheet.

Pytex is made from post-consumer recycled polyester fiber and received Global Recycled Standard (GRS) certification in 2025. After needle punching, it is heat-set at high temperature and embossed, which the company says gives it the abrasion resistance and dimensional stability for reuse after an event. The waterproof composite sheet combines a protective nonwoven, a thermoplastic elastomer (TPE) waterproof layer and a cushion nonwoven. Bokwang handles fiber blending, lamination and coating in the same plant, so it can tailor color, width, weight and function to each order.

Founded in 1983 and incorporated in 2000, the company runs seven production lines and has 16 employees. Revenue rose from KRW 4.4 billion (about USD 3.1 million) in 2022 to KRW 5.6 billion in 2025. It holds three registered patents and two design registrations, integrated ISO 9001, 14001 and 45001 certification, and is a woman-owned business. In 2026 it was selected for the Large-SME Win-Win Smart Factory program, under which it is building a manufacturing execution system (MES), and it plans to complete it by January 2027.

Bokwang has no direct exports. Event red carpet was exported indirectly through a Korean trading company in 2022 and 2025, the latter to the United States. In 2025 and 2026 it was selected for KOTRA's export-company development program. At INDEX'26, the international nonwovens exhibition in Geneva, in May 2026 it held consultations with 38 companies, and it plans to exhibit at ANEX 2027, the Asian nonwovens exhibition in Seoul in June 2027.

Its targets are North America, Europe and Asia, and it is seeking local distributors that serve exhibition, stage, landscaping and waterproofing contractors, as well as importers able to handle standard roll products in steady volumes. The company says finding the right overseas buyers for business-to-business products is its main difficulty, and that a matching program with contractors and distributors would help most.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
